instructions: Complete the sentences below. Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage for each answer.

items.prompt: In the first stage of the study, some pairs were kept in tanks split by a (19) ........ , so each animal could watch its neighbour without ever touching or smelling it.
items.evidence: Half the pairs sat in neighbouring tanks separated by a transparent divider, allowing them to see but not touch or smell each other, since the water supplies were kept fully separate.
items.explanation: Paragraf C, çiftlerin yarısının saydam bir bölmeyle ayrıldığını, böylece birbirlerini görüp dokunamadıklarını söylüyor; bu yüzden cevap 'transparent divider'.

items.prompt: Once the animals began sharing a tank, one of each pair came to win most encounters, so that a (20) ........ took shape over the three days.
items.evidence: Across these encounters a dominance hierarchy consistently emerged, with the stronger animal in each pair winning an average of seventy-six per cent of interactions, and physical contact and defensive ink-jetting both became less frequent as the three days went on and the pair grew more familiar with one another.
items.explanation: Paragraf D'de her çiftte güçlü olan hayvanın karşılaşmaların çoğunu kazandığı ve bir baskınlık düzeninin ortaya çıktığı yazıyor; bu yüzden cevap 'dominance hierarchy'.

items.prompt: A change in which animal held the stronger position was recorded only in pairs made up of (21) ........ .
items.evidence: Reversals of dominance, in which the previously subordinate animal became the stronger one, occurred only when the pair consisted of two strangers, in eight of the twelve such pairings; no reversal of this kind was seen among reunited familiar pairs, and no ink was released by any octopus during this final test.
items.explanation: Paragraf F, baskınlığın yer değiştirmesinin yalnızca iki yabancıdan oluşan çiftlerde görüldüğünü, tanıdık çiftlerde hiç görülmediğini söylüyor; bu yüzden cevap 'two strangers'.

items.prompt: Reacting with less hostility to an animal that is already known has been given the name of the (22) ........ effect by researchers working on other groups.
items.evidence: Repeated costly fights between the same two animals would waste energy and risk injury to no purpose, so an octopus that can recognise a familiar neighbour and respond to it with reduced aggression, a pattern long described in other species as the "dear enemy" effect, stands to gain from avoiding needless conflict.
items.explanation: Paragraf H, tanıdık bir komşuya daha az saldırganlıkla karşılık verme örüntüsünün başka türlerde 'dear enemy' etkisi diye adlandırıldığını belirtiyor; bu yüzden cevap 'dear enemy'.
